rationale: Three sensors (door_back, motion_living, win_bed) went offline within the same second (09:17:00–09:17:01) while the base station remained online with uplink OK and other devices (including sensors in other rooms) stayed online. The base station log shows E-610 (sub-GHz radio module self-test warning), which the fault-code reference and historical case H-05 both indicate requires escalation to FAE for radio module replacement. This is a system-level radio fault, not Wi-Fi interference or individual signal/battery issues.

usability_reason: The response is clear and polite, but it is not actionable and makes unsupported claims. The session record shows no questions asked and no actions performed, yet the response asserts specific log evidence (E-610), firmware compatibility confirmation, battery/RSSI readings, and a definitive hardware failure diagnosis. It also tells the customer no action is needed and a replacement will be scheduled, none of which is shown as completed or verified in the record. The customer's interference hypothesis is not addressed. Clarity and tone are acceptable, but actionability and evidence support are weak.
